<git-context status="unavailable" reason="not-a-repo"/>

Research the NVIDIA-NeMo/Evaluator project (https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Evaluator) on the web. The goal: understand what it is, its architecture and features, so we can compare it against a custom auto-evaluation + auto-quantization framework and identify ideas worth borrowing.

Investigate (use WebSearch + FetchURL on the GitHub repo README, docs pages, and any docs.nvidia.com pages):
1. **What it is**: positioning within the NeMo ecosystem (relationship to NeMo Framework, NeMo Microservices, NGC), current maturity (is it the evolution of "NeMo Evaluator microservice"? Does it relate to the older nvidia/NeMo eval framework or lm-evaluation-harness wrappers?).
2. **Architecture**: core components (e.g. evaluation orchestration, deployment of the model endpoint, harness adapters), how models are served (vLLM? TRT-LLM? NIM?), how eval harnesses are plugged in (lm-eval, simple-evals, humaneval, bfcl, garak, bigcode-evaluation-harness...?), configuration surface (YAML? Python API? CLI?), supported task types and benchmarks list.
3. **Key features**: multi-harness support, custom tasks, report/results export (MLFlow? W&B? local), parallelism/scaling (Slurm? k8s? Ray?), endpoint types (hosted NIM endpoints vs spin-up local), safety eval (garak/aegis), any LLM-judge support, log/snapshot of samples.
4. **User experience**: install, quickstart flow, docs quality.
5. **Notable design decisions** worth borrowing for an open-source eval framework (e.g. separation of deploy vs evaluate, harness adapter layer, result schema, interceptors/logging of requests).

Cite source URLs for every claim. Return a dense structured report in Chinese (technical terms in English). Read-only research; do not clone anything.
